entries.name: ZP6590
entries.stage: Recruiting Early Phase 1; first-in-human injection study
entries.summary: ZP6590 is an investigational long-acting GIP receptor agonist designed for co-formulation with other peptides. A sponsor-submitted record describes an 88-participant (estimated) first-in-human study of ZP6590 injections versus placebo, with an actual 9 July 2026 start. The record lists recruitment in Germany and no posted results.
entries.ukAuthorisation: The reviewed research sources do not establish UK marketing authorisation for ZP6590.
entries.nhsEngland: No NICE recommendation or NHS England access is established by these research sources.
entries.supply: Recruitment at a German research site does not establish lawful UK retail supply, pharmacy stock or sale by SHIFT.
entries.limitations: The pipeline page still calls first-in-human initiation the next step, although its Phase 1 label, the registry and Zealand’s 13 August 2026 announcement show the trial has started. The September 2027 completion and enrolment are estimates. This dose-escalation study assesses safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics; recruitment is not proof of efficacy or safety. Co-formulation is a development aim, and preclinical combination and antiemetic findings are not human combination benefits.
